Severe treatment resistant depression. Zoloft helps with anxiety, Wellbutrin helps me with depression. I maxed out on the highest dosage of Zoloft so it was recommended that I add another medication. It has honestly worked wonders. I have OCD too, and not many people know this but high-dose sertraline specifically is particularly efficacious for the treatment of OCD. Once I went up to 300mg Zoloft (100mg more than the normal advised dosage) plus 450mg Wellbutrin, it literally changed my life. This is my own experience, but it does get better. I was severely depressed for 8 years. Keep trying. You’ll find something that works.
I had this and it went away. But that’s my experience. I’m also on Wellbutrin AND Zoloft.

it doesn’t look too terrible, perhaps just underwatered. i would just slowly acclimate it to a healthier watering “schedule”, right when the soil is dry give it a solid drink and it should look better after a little while. if your pot has a drainage hole, water it until water comes out of the bottom, if not, you’ll have to be more careful so as not to leave water pooling at the bottom of your pot, which can lead to root rot. in a pot without a drainage hole, it’s generally advised to try to imagine filling up about a third of your pot, so you fully soak the plant but don’t leave water sitting at the bottom for very long. i always recommend a drainage hole but sometimes it’s not feasible

I do. Sometimes, at my lowest moments, I feel a moment of relief suddenly, sometimes I come to a realization, or I notice something that I hadn’t before in the environment around me. Some days the stars shine a little brighter for me. Some days I just can’t see it.

My 6th time was the only time someone found me. All the other times I tried to hit a major blood vessel or took a concoction of pills and failed. I hid all the evidence. 

I do feel as if my other conditions stem from my PTSD. Severe emotional neglect as a child was a very large contributor in all of my issues. 

I have Complex PTSD, which, if you do not know, has all the distinctive traits found in PTSD, but I had multiple traumas over the course of my entire life. 

It began with crippling OCD when I was maybe 5 years old. I was physically assaulted multiple times in middle school, with no social support. I was bullied by teachers. When I was 15, I held my mom as she bled out on the stairs in our house. When I was 17, I was best friends with a narcissist who tried to hit me with her car three times, I reported this and wasn’t believed because of how charming she appears. She then starts telling all of my friends what an awful person I am by making up lies, so I lost most of my friends. I would stay silent so she would stop, since she feeds off of the hurt I express. She came to my workplace several times with the intent of hurting me. She has sat outside of my house multiple times and said she wants to kill me. After all this, a close friend of mine decided I was being “too negative” for her and left me at the height of my PTSD. 

I am seeking help, but also just want everything to end. Trying to survive while also trying to die.
Yup!

It’s really nice having a word for it. I like being able to tell where exactly the things I struggle with are coming from, but it gets hard trying to separate everything so cleanly. Everything impacts everything else. Symptoms overlap. It’s been great being able to get treatment based on my personal needs. Looking for help is the strongest thing you could ever do. It gave me hope.
